stages.title: CONCEPTUAL GRAMMAR OF GOD-CONCEPTS
stages.terms: It distinguishes divine nature (personal, impersonal or transpersonal), predication (cataphatic, apophatic and analogical), attributes, reference, and the God–world and God–man relations of transcendence and immanence.
stages.mechanism: Conceptual grammar is the checklist used to identify what a tradition means by “God” before asking whether that God exists.
stages.consequence: It distinguishes divine nature (personal, impersonal or transpersonal), predication (cataphatic, apophatic and analogical), attributes, reference, and the God–world and God–man relations of transcendence and immanence.
stages.trap: A notion of God must be examined as a structured metaphysical model—nature, attributes, world-relation and human-relation—rather than as an undefined sacred name; conceptual clarification therefore precedes proof.
stages.answer: A notion of God must be examined as a structured metaphysical model—nature, attributes, world-relation and human-relation—rather than as an undefined sacred name; conceptual clarification therefore precedes proof.

stages.title: THEISM, DEISM, PANTHEISM AND PANENTHEISM
stages.terms: Theism affirms a distinct personal creator and sustainer; deism a creator-lawgiver without continuing special intervention; pantheism God–world or God–Nature identity; and panentheism the world's inclusion in God while God exceeds the world.
stages.mechanism: These four models differ over whether God creates the world, withdraws from it, includes it, or is identical with it.
stages.consequence: Theism affirms a distinct personal creator and sustainer; deism a creator-lawgiver without continuing special intervention; pantheism God–world or God–Nature identity; and panentheism the world's inclusion in God while God exceeds the world.
stages.trap: Theism, deism, pantheism and panentheism are rival grammars of dependence: they respectively affirm sustaining distinction, non-intervention after creation, identity, and inclusion-with-divine-excess.
stages.answer: Theism, deism, pantheism and panentheism are rival grammars of dependence: they respectively affirm sustaining distinction, non-intervention after creation, identity, and inclusion-with-divine-excess.

stages.title: DIVINE ATTRIBUTES AND THEIR COHERENCE
stages.terms: The classical perfect-being model combines aseity, necessity, eternity, immutability, simplicity, omnipotence, omniscience and omnibenevolence, and tests their compossibility with freedom, evil, temporal action and personal responsiveness.
stages.mechanism: Divine-attribute theory asks what perfections belong to God and whether they can consistently belong to one being.
stages.consequence: The classical perfect-being model combines aseity, necessity, eternity, immutability, simplicity, omnipotence, omniscience and omnibenevolence, and tests their compossibility with freedom, evil, temporal action and personal responsiveness.
stages.trap: The philosophical task is not to catalogue divine attributes but to test whether maximal power, complete knowledge, perfect goodness, eternity and simplicity form a coherent package.
stages.answer: The philosophical task is not to catalogue divine attributes but to test whether maximal power, complete knowledge, perfect goodness, eternity and simplicity form a coherent package.

stages.title: SPINOZA'S NOTION OF GOD
stages.terms: It is an impersonal, radically immanent conception commonly classified as pantheistic—qualified because God is the one infinite substance, not merely the aggregate of finite things; attributes express its essence and finite beings are modes.
stages.mechanism: Spinoza's notion of God is called substance monism: everything that exists is in the one infinite reality, God or Nature.
stages.consequence: It is an impersonal, radically immanent conception commonly classified as pantheistic—qualified because God is the one infinite substance, not merely the aggregate of finite things; attributes express its essence and finite beings are modes.
stages.trap: Spinoza replaces the personal creator with Deus sive Natura: one self-explanatory infinite substance whose attributes and modes unfold by necessity, gaining metaphysical unity at the cost of providential personality and libertarian freedom.
stages.answer: Spinoza replaces the personal creator with Deus sive Natura: one self-explanatory infinite substance whose attributes and modes unfold by necessity, gaining metaphysical unity at the cost of providential personality and libertarian freedom.

stages.title: ADVAITA VEDANTA'S NOTION OF GOD
stages.terms: This is non-dualism structured by two standpoints: nirguṇa Brahman is ultimate at the pāramārthika level, whereas saguṇa Īśvara is the omniscient Lord at the vyāvahārika level; plurality arises through māyā, adhyāsa and vivarta without real change in Brahman.
stages.mechanism: Advaita teaches one non-dual Brahman, while personal Īśvara is that same reality understood in relation to the empirical world.
stages.consequence: This is non-dualism structured by two standpoints: nirguṇa Brahman is ultimate at the pāramārthika level, whereas saguṇa Īśvara is the omniscient Lord at the vyāvahārika level; plurality arises through māyā, adhyāsa and vivarta without real change in Brahman.
stages.trap: Advaita preserves an empirically valid personal God while locating ultimacy in nirguṇa Brahman; its strength is non-dual absoluteness, but its pressure lies in explaining māyā, devotion and the reality of suffering.
stages.answer: Advaita preserves an empirically valid personal God while locating ultimacy in nirguṇa Brahman; its strength is non-dual absoluteness, but its pressure lies in explaining māyā, devotion and the reality of suffering.

stages.title: RAMANUJA'S VISISTADVAITA NOTION OF GOD
stages.terms: Viśiṣṭādvaita is an organic personal theism: Īśvara is the independent whole, cit and acit are real dependent qualifications, and the śarīra–śarīrī plus apṛthak-siddhi relations preserve distinction, inseparability and divine immanence.
stages.mechanism: Rāmānuja's qualified non-dualism presents one personal Brahman whose unity genuinely includes distinct souls and matter.
stages.consequence: Viśiṣṭādvaita is an organic personal theism: Īśvara is the independent whole, cit and acit are real dependent qualifications, and the śarīra–śarīrī plus apṛthak-siddhi relations preserve distinction, inseparability and divine immanence.
stages.trap: Rāmānuja reconciles unity with real plurality by treating souls and world as the dependent body of a personal Brahman, thereby grounding devotion without reducing difference to illusion.
stages.answer: Rāmānuja reconciles unity with real plurality by treating souls and world as the dependent body of a personal Brahman, thereby grounding devotion without reducing difference to illusion.

stages.title: NYAYA'S NOTION OF GOD
stages.terms: This is pluralistic realist theism: Īśvara is a special eternal self and nimitta-kāraṇa (efficient cause), while atoms are material causes; God coordinates adṛṣṭa, cosmic order, dissolution and Vedic authorship without becoming the world.
stages.mechanism: Therefore Nyaya does not teach creation ex nihilo or a real transformation of God into the world.
stages.consequence: Therefore Nyaya does not teach creation ex nihilo or a real transformation of God into the world.
stages.trap: God, selves, atoms, space and time are real; they are not appearances of one undifferentiated Absolute.
stages.answer: Nyāya's God is an efficient, not material, cause: Īśvara supplies intelligent cosmic and moral coordination while preserving the independent reality of atoms, selves, space, time and karma.

stages.title: THE HINDU POLYTHEISM DEBATE
stages.terms: The classification problem requires separating polytheism, henotheism, kathenotheism, monolatry, sectarian monotheism and metaphysical monism, because ritual plurality and claims about ultimate reality operate at different levels.
stages.mechanism: The debate asks whether Hindu plurality is best described as many independent gods, one chosen supreme deity, or diverse forms of one ultimate reality.
stages.consequence: The classification problem requires separating polytheism, henotheism, kathenotheism, monolatry, sectarian monotheism and metaphysical monism, because ritual plurality and claims about ultimate reality operate at different levels.
stages.trap: Calling Hinduism simply polytheistic is descriptively possible at the level of many deities but philosophically incomplete, since henotheistic invocation, sectarian monotheism and monistic or qualified-non-dual interpretations coexist.
stages.answer: Calling Hinduism simply polytheistic is descriptively possible at the level of many deities but philosophically incomplete, since henotheistic invocation, sectarian monotheism and monistic or qualified-non-dual interpretations coexist.

stages.title: MADHVA, SAIVA AND SAKTA NOTIONS OF GOD
stages.terms: Madhva's Dvaita affirms svatantra Viṣṇu and pañca-bheda; Śaiva Siddhānta distinguishes pati, paśu and pāśa; Kashmir Śaivism interprets the world as Śiva–Śakti's real ābhāsa; and Śākta traditions identify supreme divinity with conscious dynamic Śakti.
stages.mechanism: each school connects a causal doctrine to bondage and liberation
stages.consequence: real difference, real manifestation and divine power replace Advaita's sublatable appearance
stages.trap: do not merge Śaiva Siddhānta with Kashmir Śaivism or reflection with identity
stages.answer: Indian theism ranges from Madhva's eternal difference through Śaiva structures of lordship and recognition to Śākta divine power, so no generic 'Hindu God' can replace school-specific metaphysics.

stages.title: COMPARATIVE GOD-WORLD-MAN RELATIONS
stages.terms: The constant matrix compares divine nature, causal status, world ontology, human dependence or identity, religious function and liberation across classical theism, deism, Spinoza, Advaita, Viśiṣṭādvaita and Nyāya.
stages.mechanism: [QUALIFICATION] Therefore, "Hinduism is polytheistic" is descriptively partial but philosophically inadequate.
stages.consequence: [QUALIFICATION] Therefore, "Hinduism is polytheistic" is descriptively partial but philosophically inadequate.
stages.trap: High-value transition: The Vedic statement "Reality is one; sages speak of it variously" is frequently used to interpret plurality as diverse naming or manifestation rather than independent rival gods.
stages.answer: A valid comparison keeps the conceptual constant fixed: identity, appearance, embodiment, inclusion and efficient causation are distinct God–world grammars with different God–man consequences.

stages.title: PHYSICAL MANIFESTATION AND ULTIMATE CAUSATION
stages.terms: It distinguishes physical embodiment, religious manifestation or incarnation, material causation and metaphysical grounding; ultimacy normally requires explanatory independence rather than spatially limited embodiment.
stages.mechanism: This issue asks whether an ultimate cause must possess or appear through a physical form in order to explain the physical world.
stages.consequence: It distinguishes physical embodiment, religious manifestation or incarnation, material causation and metaphysical grounding; ultimacy normally requires explanatory independence rather than spatially limited embodiment.
stages.trap: Physical manifestation may make divine agency religiously accessible, but it is not a necessary condition of ultimate causation, because the ground of physical reality cannot itself depend on the same limiting physical conditions without further explanation.
stages.answer: Physical manifestation may make divine agency religiously accessible, but it is not a necessary condition of ultimate causation, because the ground of physical reality cannot itself depend on the same limiting physical conditions without further explanation.

stages.title: CRITICAL SYNTHESIS OF COMPETING GOD-MODELS
stages.terms: It evaluates personal versus impersonal ultimacy, transcendence versus immanence, attribute coherence, world status, freedom, evil, devotion and causation through objection–reply–residual-pressure analysis.
stages.mechanism: Final verdict: Comparison is strongest when each position is judged through the same axes of ultimate reality, world relation, human relation, causation and religious function.
stages.consequence: High-value transition: Every familiar cause is encountered through some effect or embodied activity.
stages.trap: 4. Advaita's Brahman is the presupposition of manifestation, not one manifested object.
stages.answer: No notion of God is cost-free: personal models strengthen agency and worship but face evil and anthropomorphism, while impersonal models secure unity and absoluteness but weaken providence, moral response and reciprocal relation.

stages.title: UPSC ANSWER WRITING FOR NOTIONS OF GOD
stages.terms: The method is directive-sensitive and uses a fixed spine: precise definition, metaphysical model, God–world and God–man relations, exact terminology, objection and reply, constant-matrix comparison, and a qualified verdict proportionate to 10, 15 or 20 marks.
stages.mechanism: High-value transition: 10 marks: personal and impersonal aspects.
stages.consequence: High-value transition: 10 marks: personal and impersonal aspects.
stages.answer: A high-scoring Notions of God answer defines the model, explains its relations and mechanism, tests it dialectically, compares through a fixed axis and ends with a qualified philosophical verdict.
